description: GFlow fine-tuning protocol for the exp2 tuned yambda_50m TIGER checkpoint (loss = L_SFT + lambda * L_GFlow). shared_with_sft_control mirrors finetune_sft_only.json so the two arms are directly comparable; the consumer scripts load THIS file as their argparse defaults, and tests/test_finetune_protocol_configs.py asserts both stay in sync.

base_matched_protocol.note: Since 2026-09-19 the comparison runs use the base-matched protocol: every GFlow arm fine-tunes on exactly the base SFT run's training examples (train_last_n 0 = no per-user subset) at the batch sizes of the SFT-only control. Data scope and batch sizes of those runs live ONLY in that file; gflow_finetune_tiger_matched.py (TIGER, all five datasets, factorized caches) and gflow_finetune_gpt2_amazon_fullhist.py (GPT-2, beauty/instruments) apply them on top of the shared/gflow blocks below. The gflow.train_last_n = 8 default and the yambda_500m / yambda_50m_factorized / gpt2_amazon blocks describe the FIRST sweeps and are kept so those runs stay reproducible.

gflow.reward_form_note: sasrec_transform/sasrec_temperature are the defaults of the LEGACY reward form. The factorized-path script also accepts --sasrec-transform exp with --sasrec-temperatures (teacher softmax, R = exp(score/T)) and --interaction-exponents (R = sasrec * interaction ** gamma) as grid dimensions applied at lookup time.

gpt2_amazon.note: Override for scripts/exp4-reward-ablations/gflow_finetune_gpt2_amazon.py only. In the first sweep (2026-09-10, 32 GB V100) every GPT-2 micro-batch scoring more than 512 candidate sequences (batch x (K+1); db/subtb add sid_len prefix passes) ran out of memory: all K=100 runs, K=10 for every objective on beauty and for db/subtb on instruments, K=3 for db/subtb. 512 keeps K=1 at the protocol 256 x 8 and shrinks the micro-batch to 128 x 16 (K=3) and 46 x 44 (K=10) with the effective batch unchanged; the script additionally halves the cap and retries on OOM (--oom-retries).

gpt2_amazon_fullhist.source_of_truth: configs/exp2-tuned-params/finetune_base_matched.json (the wrapper reads that file; this block mirrors it and tests assert they agree). Since 2026-09-19 the GPT-2 arms run the same grid, K, schedule, seeds and curriculum as TIGER; the note below describes the earlier 128 x 16 / K=3 setup.
gpt2_amazon_fullhist.note: Defaults of scripts/exp4-reward-ablations/gflow_finetune_gpt2_amazon_fullhist.py (the wrapper holds them as constants; tests assert the two agree). train_last_n 0 = both arms (GFlow runs and the SFT-only control) fine-tune on the FULL user history, every prefix example: beauty 131,413, instruments 116,989. The last-8 subset of the gflow block is a yambda-scale cache constraint and does not apply here (full-history float16 caches are ~3.2 GB / ~2.0 GB per component). Batch sizes match the TIGER fine-tuning on Amazon: effective train batch 2048 (accumulated as 128 x 16 at K=3 under the 512-candidate cap, identically in the SFT-only control via uniform_micro_batch), validation batch 64 (sft_finetune_control default for Amazon), final-eval batch 64 (tiger.test_eval_batch_size). Own output root, cache root, and metrics CSV (gflow_finetune_gpt2_amazon_fullhist_metrics_summary.csv).

known_deviations_from_sft_control.loss: L_SFT + lambda * L_GFlow with lambda from one-time gradient-norm calibration (control: L_SFT only)
known_deviations_from_sft_control.train_subset: fine-tunes on the last 8 train examples per user (69,495 examples) instead of the control's full last-128 layout (993,926) — the dense full-catalog reward caches would be ~224 GB per combo otherwise. The datamodule keeps the full layout so the catalog matches the checkpoint. RESOLVED in the base-matched rerun (gflow_finetune_tiger_matched.py, factorized caches, --train-last-n 0): both arms train on the full last-128 layout.
known_deviations_from_sft_control.batch_scaling: for large negative counts the micro-batch shrinks so batch*(K+1) <= max_candidate_batch, with grad accumulation keeping the effective batch at 2048
known_deviations_from_sft_control.yambda_500m_caches: yambda_500m stores per-component factors instead of dense rows (dense rows would be ~0.5 TB per cache); combos/powers are composed at lookup time (ComposedFactorizedRewardCache, exact logZ).
known_deviations_from_sft_control.yambda_500m_monitor: yambda_500m gflow runs validate on a FIXED 25% sample; the finished SFT-control runs used a re-drawn one (only the in-training monitor differs; final evaluation is on the full splits in both arms). RESOLVED in the base-matched rerun: sft_finetune_control_matched.py draws the same fixed sample (val_sample_resample false, seed 0).

protocol_history.runs_before_2026-08-27: used validate_every=1, max_grad_norm=1.0, amp_dtype=bfloat16 (each run's resolved_config.json records its actual values); aligned to the SFT control when this file became the defaults source
protocol_history.runs_before_2026-09-15: did not score the init checkpoint (run_validation_at_start=false): best_val/best.pt were the best post-training validation even when worse than the init, and patience counted from that epoch (a run whose best was epoch 14 stopped at epoch 64). Since 2026-09-15 the init is validated first (best_epoch -1) and is the patience reference; each run's resolved_config.json records which rule it used.
protocol_history.yambda_500m_runs_before_2026-09-15: started from trials/dropout-0/best.pt (the 8-epoch OFAT tuning snapshot) while the imported init baseline was measured on the converged promoted best.pt; those runs are stale (the script now moves them aside and re-runs) and must not be compared with the init rows.
protocol_history.yambda_500m_runs_before_2026-09-18: validated on a RE-DRAWN 25% sample (trainer default val_sample_resample=true): best_epoch/early stopping were decided by the draw (epoch 14 in every cell, stop at 65). Final full-split metrics of those runs are valid for cross-cell comparison (same epoch, same draws) but each checkpoint is likely not the run's optimum. The 500m SFT control still uses re-drawing.

yambda_500m.note: Override block for scripts/exp4-reward-ablations/gflow_finetune_yambda500m.py only. train_last_n keeps the 50m per-user tail rule (~0.70M of the 9.9M-example last-128 layout); val_sample_fraction 0.25 is the yambda_500m SFT-control's in-training monitor rule (final evaluation uses the full 87k-row splits). Rewards come from FACTORIZED per-component caches (precompute_reward_factors.py, hidden states stored as float16) composed at lookup time, so no --store-power-sums and no dense per-combo caches exist for 500m. val_sample_resample false (since 2026-09-18): the 25% monitor sample is drawn once and reused; with re-drawing, all 24 first-sweep cells picked epoch 14 and all four SFT-control runs epoch 55, because the draw's seed depends only on the step count and draw noise (sd ~0.0017 NDCG@5) exceeds the plateau's epoch-to-epoch change.

tiger_beauty.note: Override block for scripts/exp4-reward-ablations/gflow_finetune_yambda500m.py --dataset beauty (TIGER, factorized caches). The Amazon datasets have no last-8 sweep: they run ONLY under the base-matched protocol (gflow_finetune_tiger_matched.py reads configs/exp2-tuned-params/finetune_base_matched.json for batch sizes, schedule and grid); train_last_n 0 here keeps even a direct call on the full user history.

tiger_beauty_2023.note: As tiger_beauty, for --dataset beauty_2023. The validation split has one example per user (662,540): the in-training monitor runs on ONE fixed 10% sample (seed 0), as yambda_500m does with 25% of 87k; the final evaluation uses the full splits.

yambda_50m_factorized.note: Override block for scripts/exp4-reward-ablations/gflow_finetune_yambda500m.py --dataset yambda_50m_listens: the 50m assets through the factorized-cache path (needed for exp(score/T) rewards, which overflow the dense float16 caches of gflow_finetune_yambda50m.py). Same per-user tail and full-split validation monitor as the 50m grid; outputs go to experiments/exp4-gflow-yambda50m-factorized and their own metrics CSV.
